figures.caption: Fig. 2: CritLens system architecture. After the user specifies a decision goal, the data processing stage segments and encodes review text into a semantic space; the modeling stage generates a prior model via an LLM, performs evidence alignment, and enters an iterative loop of criteria discovery and weight adjustment; the decision output stage performs scoring, ranking, and report generation. Four visual analytics views on the right span the entire workflow, supporting exploration, diagnosis, and verification at each stage.

Fig. 6: User study Likert scale results (n = 8, 5-point scale). Bar charts are center-aligned at the neutral option, with negative ratings on the left and positive on the right. Dashed lines separate the four evaluation dimensions.

Fig. 4: Case Study 1. (A) Lasso selection over uncovered regions in explore mode; keywords reveal printhead-related topics. (B) Another cluster points to mechanical jams and paper handling failures. (C) Beeswarm plots show that top-5 products still have many 1-star reviews. (D) Score evolution ribbon chart tracking ranking changes across 13 iterations; top 3 stabilize in later rounds.

Fig. 5: Case Study 2. (A) Four zero-match criteria are deleted. (B) Weight adjustment: reducing C1, increasing C5. (C) Consistency repair: C3’s CR drops from 0.183 to 0.080. (D) Criterion scores and beeswarm plot comparison for the top-3 hotels.
